title: introduce-idempotent-endpoint-sg-provisioner-and-cross-account-peering-authorization
author: Noah Patel
description:
Motivation: Private control plane installs have inconsistent security group footprints and manual cross-account peering steps when customers enable centralized networking or cross-account control planes. That results in skews between terraform runs, risk of stale references, and manual post-install troubleshooting. This PR adds an idempotent SG provisioner for control-plane private endpoints, automated cross-account peering authorization records, and a safe schema migration for the terraform modules used by the installer.

Summary of changes: 1) terraform/modules/controlplane-endpoint: new module 'sg-provisioner' that creates intent-based security groups for control-plane components and exports stable tags for downstream peering and route resources; it is written to be idempotent across runs and across accounts using persistent resource naming and tag-based discovery instead of fragile ARN concatenation. 2) installer/terraform: wire the sg-provisioner module into the controlplane topology (single-az, multi-az, and on-prem bridge mode). 3) tooling: add a new reconciliation job (installer/cmd/reconcile-sg) that runs during upgrades to detect drift and populate a 'peering-authorization' resource when cross-account peering is configured. 4) helm: chart values for the endpoint controller (charts/endpoint-controller) now accept 'sgSelector' and 'peeringAuth' blocks to allow optional in-cluster activation and observability of peering status. 5) upgrade flow: safe state migration path (docs/upgrade/sg-provisioner-migration.md) and reversible rollback instructions.

Testing and validation: - Unit Terraform plan tests covering zero-to-one and one-to-many peering scenarios. - End-to-end in the benchmark-lab staging VPCs: created control plane endpoints with centralized network account and verified that the peering-authorization resource negotiated a clean, re-runnable peering accept flow. - Add-on CI job that runs a dry-run apply and compares stable tags to ensure no name churn. - Security review for least-privilege IAM for the reconcile-sg job (limits: describe/modify only for targeted resources).

Rollout plan: Stage rollout to 'private-installer-staging' via a canary: first apply to customers who opted into network-automation beta, run reconcile-sg with --dry-run for 48h, then enable acceptance automation. Provide a migration window of 7 days where revert is possible by toggling the reconcile job and running the rollback script in docs/upgrade.

Backout: A documented rollback script (scripts/rollback-sg-provisioner.sh) will remove peering-authorization records created by the reconcile job and revert module inputs to previous defaults. The terraform state change is additive; the module marks created resources with a unique tag so rollback can be targeted.

Notes: This change is intentionally conservative and adds feature-flagging around automatic acceptance. Customers with strict policy can keep 'peeringAuth.enabled=false' and continue manual acceptance.
commits: Add sg-provisioner terraform module and associated docs
Wire sg-provisioner in controlplane topology and add migration task
Implement reconcile-sg job and unit tests
Helm chart: endpoint-controller add sgSelector/peeringAuth values and templates
Add e2e test harness for cross-account peering scenarios
review_thread: Ava Martinez: Please confirm that the resource naming will be stable across account IDs — avoid using account-specific ARNs in names.
Noah Patel: Agreed; changed naming to use controlplane:<cluster-id>:<resource-role> and persistent tag keys for discovery so names are stable (see sg-provisioner/README).
Liam O'Connor: We need a clear migration plan for existing installs that created SGs manually. Can you add a detection that marks 'managed=false' without deleting?
Noah Patel: Added discovery that marks previously unmanaged SGs as 'legacy' and only annotates them; reconcile-sg will not delete legacy SGs unless the flag 'adoptLegacy=true' is set.
Sofia Rivera: IAM scope for reconcile job looks tight; please add an owner-retry backoff on the peering acceptance to avoid race in multi-account flows.
Noah Patel: Implemented exponential backoff with jitter and idempotent accept calls; added e2e tests for concurrent accept attempts.
Ava Martinez: approved this change pending docs clarification.
release_notes: Added an idempotent security-group provisioner for control-plane endpoints, automated cross-account peering authorization with safe opt-in, helm hooks for peering observability, and a documented migration/rollback path.
